title: Keep a copy
hints: A C string needs one byte more than `strlen` says: the terminating `'\0'` has to live somewhere too.
Handle `NULL` first. Then `malloc(strlen(s) + 1)`, check the result for `NULL`, and copy the bytes including the terminator.
`if (s == NULL) return NULL; size_t n = strlen(s) + 1; char *copy = malloc(n); if (copy == NULL) return NULL; memcpy(copy, s, n); return copy;`
